mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 4 Series 430i engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 4 Series 430i engine replacement typically costs between £3,800 and £6,000 for a reconditioned unit, with rebuilt engines ranging from £5,000 to £8,000. Used engines start from around £2,000. These prices are supply-only - fitting adds 10-14 hours of labour at specialist rates (£650-£910).

mainEntity.name: What are the common problems with the BMW 4 Series 430i B48 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The B48 engine in the 430i is generally reliable, but there are some well-documented issues to be aware of. The most common are coolant system leaks (oil filter housing and coolant flange), timing chain tensioner wear, and carbon buildup on intake valves due to direct injection.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 4 Series 430i?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on your car's value and condition. For a 2016-2020 BMW 4 Series 430i worth £8,000-£22,000, a rebuilt engine at £5,000-£8,000 is a significant investment but often worthwhile if the car is otherwise in good condition. For cars under £8,000, carefully evaluate whether a repair or used engine makes more financial sense.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the BMW 4 Series 430i and 420i engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both the 430i and 420i use the same B48 2.0-litre turbocharged petrol engine, but the 430i is tuned for higher output. The 430i produces 245-252bhp, while the 420i produces approximately 181-184bhp. The engines share the same basic architecture, but the 430i features different engine calibration and turbocharger mapping.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 4 Series 430i engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 4 Series 430i engine replacement typically takes 2-3 days for a specialist workshop to complete, assuming the replacement engine is already in stock. This includes removal of the old engine, fitting the replacement, and full system testing.

acceptedAnswer.text: Every rebuilt and reconditioned engine supplied through EnginesMarket carries a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. The B48 is a robust, well-engineered unit when properly maintained. historyTimeline.h2: BMW 4 Series 430i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 4 Series 430i arrived in 2016 as a replacement for the 428i, introducing the new B48 engine family across the 4 Series range. It was offered across all three body styles - Coupe (F32), Convertible (F33) and Gran Coupe (F36) - and continued into the second-generation G22 (2020 onwards) with updated B48TU powerplants.

Second-generation G22 4 Series launched; 430i continues with updated B48TU engine

commonProblems.h2: BMW 4 Series 430i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 4 Series 430i is powered exclusively by the B48 engine family - a 2.0-litre turbocharged petrol unit that replaced the earlier N20. While the B48 is generally considered more reliable than its predecessor, it has its own set of well-documented issues. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Coolant System Leaks - Oil Filter Housing and Coolant Flange Failure
problems.rootCause: The B48 engine uses plastic components in the cooling system, including the oil filter housing and coolant flange. Over time, these plastic parts can crack due to heat cycling, leading to coolant leaks. A slow leak can go unnoticed until the system runs low, causing overheating and potential engine damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace oil filter housing and gaskets; system flush and refill
repairOptions.longevity: If caught early; aluminium aftermarket parts available for improved durability

For cars valued £10,000-£16,000, a reconditioned engine replacement is viable if you plan to keep the car 2+ years. problems.recommendation: For BMW 4 Series 430i models, regular cooling system inspections are essential. The plastic oil filter housing and coolant flange are known weak points - upgrading to aluminium aftermarket parts when replacement is needed can prevent recurrence. If you notice coolant loss or warning lights, have the system inspected immediately. Full engine replacement is rarely required for cooling system issues alone - only consider it if the engine has sustained additional damage from overheating.
